note: Every input carries a basis tag. 'verified' = read on an official source (sourceId given). 'client' = supplied by the client and reproduced as-is (may be unverified). 'assumption' = set by this model because no official figure can answer the question; each carries a range and is stress-tested in the Sensitivity table. Nothing here is presented as a fact about the future. Central case deliberately avoids optimistic inputs: appreciation 3.5% (below the 35-year CA HPI rate) and portfolio return 6.0% (below long-run equity returns).

inputs.note: Post-2025 repricing environment; the FAIR Plan's approved average increase of 29.1% effective 2026‑10‑15 is far above CPI. CDI data (S33/S34) is the only official premium series and it ends in 2017.

inputs.note: Three-unit pre-1979 building: more roof, plumbing, paint and turnover work.

Market rent for B's vacant unit (1-bedroom benchmark)
inputs.note: HUD FY2026 Small Area FMR for ZIP 94122, 1-bedroom. Conservative choice: the 2-bedroom benchmark is $3,310.

inputs.note: HUD FY2026 Small Area FMR for ZIP 95014, 2-bedroom. The 3-bedroom benchmark is $5,870; the bedroom count of the house is unknown, so the lower figure is used. Flagged I8.

inputs.note: SF Rent Board allowable annual increase 1.6% for 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28; SF Administrative Code ch. 37. Conservative: ignores vacancy decontrol on turnover.

inputs.label: Property A rent growth (single-family home, not rent-capped)
inputs.note: Civ. Code §1947.12(d)(5) exempts separately-alienable single-family homes owned by a natural person from the AB 1482 cap (S07), so A can track market rent.

inputs.label: Vacancy and credit loss on rented units
inputs.note: SF rent-controlled tenancies are long, so losses are low, but turnover and bad debt are real.

inputs.label: After-tax return on a reinvested portfolio
inputs.note: Nominal, after federal and California tax drag on a balanced equity/fixed-income portfolio, before advisory fees. Not an official figure; it is the discount-rate challenger to real estate. A 6.0% central case is deliberately below the long-run US equity return.

Cost of sale (commission, escrow, title, transfer tax)
inputs.note: Commissions are negotiable, so no official rate exists. Includes the county documentary transfer tax of 0.11% (S06) and, for San Francisco, the 0.75% city tier for $1M-$5M sales.
